first_impression.reaction: Hashtags are not my department, but my daughter sent it, so I read it properly. The first line is sensible and plain: 'A good wedding hashtag is short, yours alone and easy for every guest to spell.' I was relieved it didn't open with slang. The second paragraph lost me a little: 'what a list of tags can't settle: one tag across a weekend abroad, and guests' photos shared the way you intend.' I had to read it twice.

journey.quote: A hashtag gathers public posts for anyone to see, so pair it with a private album and ask guests to check before they share photos of other people or their children.
journey.reaction: This is the bit I actually care about. I didn't know the tag made the photos public. My sister's grandchildren will be there and I would not want them all over the internet. Good that it's up the top.

journey.section: What makes a good wedding hashtag
journey.quote: A guest who hears it once from the MC should type it correctly first time.
journey.reaction: Common sense. Half our family would get a clever spelling wrong.

journey.quote: Sue and Ed joined as #sueed reads as "sued", which no couple wants on a welcome sign.
journey.reaction: That made me laugh, and it's exactly the sort of thing nobody notices until the signs are printed and paid for.

journey.quote: #SamAndAlexRivera: the full names, clear for older guests.
journey.reaction: Thank you. Someone remembered the older guests without making it sound like we're a nuisance.

journey.quote: Keep a funny tag kind: your grandparents will see it on a sign.
journey.reaction: Quite right. I'd underline this one for my daughter.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: One person to deal with is what I want. But 'payments' is where I sit up. Whose account do the deposits go into, and what happens if a supplier over there folds? The page doesn't say.

journey.quote: Australia's eSafety Commissioner advises that you should always ask for consent before sharing a photo or video.
journey.reaction: Quoting the eSafety Commissioner rather than someone's opinion. That reassures me and I'd forward this section to my husband.

journey.quote: The Act doesn't cover individuals, so it doesn't apply to a photo taken by someone acting in a personal capacity.
journey.reaction: I read this twice. 'Acting in a personal capacity' is lawyer talk. I think it means a guest snapping away for themselves, but say so.

journey.quote: A line beside your hashtag on the welcome sign does a lot of work: please ask before you post anyone else, check with parents before sharing children, and we will remove any photo on request.
journey.reaction: Good idea, I'd want that on the sign. But 'post anyone else' and 'sharing children' read oddly, as if we're posting the children themselves. If it's going on a sign it should be worded properly.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Now we're talking. Fee in writing, Australian dollars, our time zone. That is the most useful sentence on the page for me.

unanswered_questions: When the Advisor handles 'payments', are the deposits protected if an overseas supplier disappears, and who is accountable?
Can I speak to someone on the phone before anything is booked? Is there a named person?
What is the difference between Wedded Concierge and a Wedded Advisor? The page says to 'begin with Wedded Concierge' but the person is the Advisor.
If something goes wrong on the day overseas, who do we ring?

turn_offs_found.quote: **#HartsOffTheMarket:** cheeky, for a crowd that enjoys a joke.
turn_offs_found.why: Not offensive, just a bit young for me. It's a passing line and the 'keep it kind' note after it makes up for it.

would_share_with: My husband (the privacy and children's photos section)
My daughter, back to her, with 'your grandparents will see it on a sign' circled

cta_reaction.quote: Tell us your date, your guest list and where you would like to marry, and begin with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: Not because of a hashtag article. But the fee in writing and AUD quotes are the right signals. I'd click once my daughter has decided on overseas, and only if I can talk to a real person before handing over any money.

top_3_changes: Replace old: "please ask before you post anyone else, check with parents before sharing children, and we will remove any photo on request." with new: "please ask before you post photos of anyone else, check with parents before sharing photos of children, and we will remove any photo on request."

Replace old: "The Act doesn't cover individuals, so it doesn't apply to a photo taken by someone acting in a personal capacity." with new: "The Act doesn't cover individuals, so it doesn't apply to a photo a guest takes in their own personal capacity."

Replace old: "Below is that method, ideas by style built from invented couples, and what a list of tags can't settle: one tag across a weekend abroad, and guests' photos shared the way you intend." with new: "Below is that method, ideas by style built from invented couples, and two things a list of tags can't settle for you: whether to use one tag across a weekend abroad, and how to help guests share photos the way you intend."

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes the draft exactly
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, plain-spoken, practical)
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and fact markers treated as invisible
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings and add no prices, names, statistics, business details, tool claims or real couples' tags

assumptions: References to Margaret's sister's grandchildren and her husband are in-character colour only, not brand facts.
Margaret is not choosing the hashtag, so relevance is naturally low; her interest is guest privacy, older relatives and who handles money.
Markdown bold markers in the turn-off quote are reproduced as written in the draft source.

open_questions.question: Should the 'payments' line near the weekend section link to anything explaining how deposits and supplier contracts are handled? I cannot suggest wording without inventing business details.
